subject.title: [Bug] MiniMax Token Plan (Max) broken in sub-agents after v5.22 bootstrap change

question: Should OpenClaw change the current MiniMax/sub-agent contracts for Token Plan users, and if so should the accepted path be provider endpoint routing, a generated-media continuation fix, or a new sub-agent skill/bootstrap inheritance surface?
rationale: Source inspection shows the reported behavior is plausible, but the permanent fix crosses provider auth, documented MiniMax endpoint behavior, sub-agent context boundaries, and optional skill/plugin ownership, so automation should not choose the product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require live proof, then fix narrowly
options.body: Keep the current bootstrap boundary, live-test Token Plan endpoint/auth behavior first, and only change provider/media code for a proven runtime bug.

options.title: Sponsor a bootstrap/role-file contract
options.body: Treat the missing Token Plan skills as part of the broader sub-agent context-control work and route it through the existing bootstrap-tier or role-file product discussions.

options.title: Keep mmx as an external workaround
options.body: Document the mmx CLI path or publish a ClawHub skill/bundle if maintainers decide Token Plan office workflows should not become core sub-agent behavior.

recommendation.title: Require live proof, then fix narrowly
recommendation.body: Keep the current bootstrap boundary, live-test Token Plan endpoint/auth behavior first, and only change provider/media code for a proven runtime bug.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing trail ties steipete to related MiniMax/Codex boundary commits and recent maintainer-side reviews on overlapping bootstrap product decisions.
